Patriot,

Every mission ends with an after-action report. What happened. What it cost. How it happened.

**[**Here's the one I refuse to write:**](http://links.harriganfornc.com/u/click?_t=687026f8d8f7415aa539c5385c376b1f&_m=e4f2350338a247d2a0d697e6197dc6f6&_e=BodUYb--xlG5fAMkpLwNJCTqyu0do3WcpASQH9YkCs8V7frZYdZPbs9MBDpE2Bw6qfQsRVEOKk8uWWZ2mOQJauu7-6QTr0iWm3P5h-kJHEXh1EbWqDGaLeNbf_JWkcno5I_d8hrpGtQB5zZzvE2fuoLnTiSq-SCXezCCep5fS3cttYBAQ6QDeZhE4xPELfORr-ZT7wb5t6O49cFg0tSbJkCZBQ_Bb0N_539uKCromRqEQe0yEnnmxyaxSLX5HB37LrktIAyeF2zv9S9f8YqxXiGiQP_X-fpYpXNuDmzo--3jnXrzvEDMqXpyZymxjBH4S3q_0mpz3-PbA9IuJpdnBnWPUiGbWl2RRfj_3KEcFkA9N1kI8GKLe41YsrBJD29VPs3s4HI4oMF2SS9k5UKBbpmNp-DiXnZxGu06Djfdq1o20ObtwWaUYM0W4C1zjhsIZ8JflnNptpJ_dUdg8FuQI6GDzNLZaAqFe8nrt5UD2KqVvjk1Zn6E2N9WaqYxPSQ7jwhMlufjAktq6KRQXjRc65zx3rmgUA_0vzU0_0ZP3_g%3D)**

**WHAT HAPPENED:** Democrats took back the House of Representatives.

**WHAT IT COSTS US:** Every committee gavel flipped to the Left, including on the Armed Services Committee, where I fight for our troops and our national defense. Our priorities stalled. Our majority was gone.

**HOW IT HAPPENED:** Not because we lost the argument. Because too many conservatives decided their vote wouldn't matter and stayed home.

It's Chris. I have news:
**Tomorrow, I 'll face John Sununu in our first debate.**
The GOP has spent over $60 million trying to buy this Senate seat.
I don't take a dime of corporate PAC money.
Our strength comes from people like you, and with just 22 days left, we need to show Sununu that New Hampshire isn't for sale.
**[Will you chip in $10 or whatever you can afford before tomorrow's debate to help us beat John Sununu and flip the Senate?](https://substack.com/redirect/260eb2fa-f3f1-498e-96ae-047b2bffb4f6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

When I first ran for Congress, I made the decision that I wouldn't take a dime of corporate PAC money.
Not because I thought it would make campaigns easier. And not because I believed everyone else had to make the same decision.
I made that commitment because I wanted Granite Staters to know exactly where my priorities would lie as their representative.
Granite Staters responded to that choice. They saw it was proof that I was serious about changing the culture in Washington.
New Hampshire is a purple state. Every race here is competitive. And over the years, I've heard more than a few people suggest that refusing corporate PAC money meant competing with one hand tied behind my back.
But four tough congressional races later, we've shown something important: You can build a winning campaign the right way.
**I believe public service is about serving the public.**
People deserve leaders who are accountable to the communities they represent -- especially in this current moment.
Now we are facing our biggest test yet: Control of the Senate could come down to New Hampshire, and Republicans and their allies are already preparing to spend millions of dollars to flip this seat.
[DONATE](https://substack.com/redirect/260eb2fa-f3f1-498e-96ae-047b2bffb4f6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Far-right billionaires, dark money groups, and organizations backed by Big Oil and Big Pharma are lining up behind my GOP opponent because they know what's at stake.
It wasn't always easy, but I still refuse to take a dime of corporate PAC money -- because independence matters. I answer to Granite Staters, not corporate PACs.
I want the people I represent to know that my focus will always be on lowering costs, protecting Social Security and Medicare, defending access to abortion, and making sure people who work hard have the opportunity to get ahead.
People deserve leaders who tell them the truth, fight for their priorities, and remember who sent them to Washington in the first place.
That's what I've tried to do throughout my time in Congress, and it's the same approach I'll bring to the U.S. Senate.
This campaign comes down to independence and making sure Granite Staters are always put first.
Thank you for reading,
Chris

I have news: Tomorrow, I 'll face John Sununu in our first debate. The GOP has spent over $60 million trying to buy this Senate seat. I don't take a dime of corporate PAC money. Our strength comes from people like you, and with just 22 days left, we need to show Sununu that New Hampshire isn't for sale. | | ---|---|--- When I first ran for Congress, I made the decision that I wouldn't take a dime of corporate PAC money. Not because I thought it would make campaigns easier. And not because I believed everyone else had to make the same decision. I made that commitment because I wanted Granite Staters to know exactly where my priorities would lie as their representative. Granite Staters responded to that choice. They saw it was proof that I was serious about changing the culture in Washington. New Hampshire is a purple state. Every race here is competitive. And over the years, I've heard more than a few people suggest that refusing corporate PAC money meant competing with one hand tied behind my back. But four tough congressional races later, we've shown something important: You can build a winning campaign the right way. I believe public service is about serving the public. People deserve leaders who are accountable to the communities they represent -- especially in this current moment. Now we are facing our biggest test yet: Control of the Senate could come down to New Hampshire, and Republicans and their allies are already preparing to spend millions of dollars to flip this seat. Far-right billionaires, dark money groups, and organizations backed by Big Oil and Big Pharma are lining up behind my GOP opponent because they know what's at stake. It wasn't always easy, but I still refuse to take a dime of corporate PAC money -- because independence matters. I answer to Granite Staters, not corporate PACs. I want the people I represent to know that my focus will always be on lowering costs, protecting Social Security and Medicare, defending access to abortion, and making sure people who work hard have the opportunity to get ahead. People deserve leaders who tell them the truth, fight for their priorities, and remember who sent them to Washington in the first place. That's what I've tried to do throughout my time in Congress, and it's the same approach I'll bring to the U.S. Senate. This campaign comes down to independence and making sure Granite Staters are always put first. Thank you for reading, Chris | | | | | | | (C) 2026 Chris Pappas PO Box 313, Manchester, NH 03105 ? ?

name: Heidi Ganahl
subject: Monday News Digest: 10/12/2026
body:
Colorado's Ballots Are Here. Are You Ready?

[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

OCTOBER 12, 2026

MONDAY NEWS DIGEST

Dear Rocky Mountain Voice family,

The countdown to Election Day is officially on.

Ballots are arriving in mailboxes across Colorado, and in just a few
short weeks, voters will decide who leads our state, who represents us
in Washington, and the future of some of Colorado's most consequential
policies.

With 22 DAYS UNTIL ELECTION DAY, we're making it our mission at Rocky
Mountain Voice to give you the information you need to make informed
decisions before casting your ballot. And we've been busy!

🗳️ _14 STATEWIDE BALLOT MEASURES. HERE'S WHAT YOU NEED TO KNOW.
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

This year's ballot is particularly interesting. Of the 14 statewide
measures, 13 were placed there through citizen petitions, rather than
by the Legislature. From taxes and TABOR to election integrity, public
safety, parental rights and energy policy, there is a LOT at stake.

Our editorial team put together a comprehensive guide explaining what
each measure would do, who's behind it, who's funding the opposition,
and what voters should consider.

One particularly interesting battle involves Amendment 87 and
Proposition 136, two competing income tax measures that could create a
legal dispute if both pass. Meanwhile, millions of dollars are flowing
into campaigns surrounding fentanyl penalties and measures involving
children and schools.

READ: WHAT'S ON YOUR 2026 COLORADO BALLOT — ALL 14 STATEWIDE
MEASURES
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

🏛️ _WEISER VS. MARX: A RARE APPEARANCE TOGETHER
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

Last Thursday, Colorado's two gubernatorial candidates, Democrat Phil
Weiser and Republican Victor Marx, appeared together at a Colorado
Chamber of Commerce luncheon.

Heidi & Tori from Team RMV attended the event and walked away with
plenty of unanswered questions. Both candidates acknowledged that
Colorado has become increasingly expensive for families and businesses
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
but their approaches differed. Marx emphasized reducing regulations,
scrutinizing government spending and protecting energy reliability,
while Weiser focused on collaboration, public investment and
environmental protections.

Unfortunately, with questions provided in advance and limited
opportunities for follow-up, the discussion felt more like prepared
campaign remarks than a meaningful debate.

READ: WEISER AND MARX SHARE RARE STAGE, BUT ADVANCE QUESTIONS YIELD
FEW SURPRISES
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

🇺🇸 _MEET COLORADO'S NEXT GENERATION OF REPUBLICAN LEADERS
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

For years, the conversation surrounding Colorado Republicans has
focused on an aging political bench and the party's struggle to
connect with younger voters. But a new generation of leaders is
emerging.

In her latest commentary, Heidi highlights young Republicans making
their mark across Colorado, including House Minority Leader Jarvis
Caldwell, Rep. Ryan Gonzalez, Senate candidate Teddy Collins, House
candidates Scott Shamblin and Jason Bias, and Rep. Dusty Johnson.

They're business owners, grassroots advocates, former campus
organizers and young Coloradans who have decided to step into public
service. Whether they're incumbents or first-time candidates, their
stories offer an interesting look at how the next generation is
approaching politics in our state.

READ: YOUNG GUNS — MEET THE NEXT GENERATION OF COLORADO REPUBLICANS
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

📬 _MORE ELECTION COVERAGE COMING THIS WEEK!_

We're not finished yet. This week, we'll be publishing additional
election coverage, including a closer look at _COLORADO'S FEDERAL
RACES_ and _JUDICIAL RETENTION QUESTIONS_—two areas of the ballot
voters shouldn't overlook.

Our goal isn't to tell you how to vote. It's to make sure you have
access to the facts, the candidates' positions and the information
necessary to make your own decisions.

In the meantime, make sure your voter registration is current, check
your ballot status at GoVoteColorado.gov
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
and share our election coverage with your friends, family and
neighbors.

_A FEW IMPORTANT DATES TO REMEMBER:_

October 12: All mail ballot drop boxes open

October 19: In-person voting centers open

October 26: Last recommended day to return ballots by mail

November 3: Election Day! Ballots must be received by 7 p.m.

Colorado's future is shaped by the decisions we make today. Let's make
sure we're informed before we make them.

In truth & liberty,
Team RMV

TOP STORIES OF THE WEEK

WHAT’S ON YOUR 2026 COLORADO BALLOT: ALL 14 STATEWIDE MEASURES
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

BY RMV EDITORIAL BOARD, ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

Colorado voters open their mail ballots this October to more
citizen-written questions than any election in half a century.
Fourteen measures. Thirteen put there by citizens gathering
signatures, one sent over by the Legislature. The total ties the
record set in 2024, 2008, and 2006, but the share driven by petition
rather than lawmakers sets this year apart.

YOUNG GUNS: MEET THE NEXT GENERATION OF COLORADO REPUBLICANS
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

BY HEIDI GANAHL, ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

_The knock on Colorado Republicans for years has been the same one: an
aging bench, a shrinking footprint, a brand that can’t connect with
younger voters in a state that keeps drifting left. That critique
might need updating._

DENVER MASK BAN DREW A FEDERAL SUIT AFTER COURTS BLOCKED 4 SIMILAR
LAWS
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

BY SHAINA COLE, ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

The U.S. Department of Justice sued Denver on Thursday over the
ordinance barring law enforcement officers from wearing masks and
requiring them to display identification, saying the city has no
authority to tell federal agents how to do their jobs.

__

STATE

WEISER AND MARX SHARE RARE STAGE, BUT ADVANCE QUESTIONS YIELD FEW
SURPRISES
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

BY TORI STORK, ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

Colorado’s two major-party candidates for governor shared the stage
Thursday at a Colorado Chamber of Commerce luncheon in Denver,
offering business leaders a chance to hear Democrat Phil Weiser and
Republican Victor Marx address the state’s mounting economic
challenges.

WEISER’S BLUEPRINT: WHAT HIS HEALTH PLAN WON’T SAY BEFORE ELECTION
DAY
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

BY SHAINA COLE, ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

Phil Weiser’s Healthy Colorado Plan runs to three pillars and more
than 1,600 words. It promises to move Colorado “from our current
‘sick care’ system to a true ‘health care’ system.” It calls
the first pillar, Primary Care for All, “a systemwide mandate."

COLORADO’S $3.1M FOR 3RS, THE FREE SEX ED CURRICULUM BEHIND THE
ROARING FORK LEGAL FIGHT
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

BY KELLY NOTARFRANCESCO, ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

The State of Colorado has awarded more than $3 million in
sex-education grants to nearly two dozen school districts and charter
schools that adopted or planned to adopt the same human sexuality
education curriculum now at the center of a legal conflict between
parents and Roaring Fork School District — a curriculum that is free
to download.

__

READ MORE STATE NEWS
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

LOCAL

ANTHONY: BOULDER SUES SUNCOR OVER CLIMATE WHILE LEASING 12,000 ACRES
TO CATTLE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

BY TOM ANTHONY, ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

_As a Christian I get use of some ancient wisdom to toss around as I
see fit. I defer to Matthew 7:5, “You hypocrite, first take the log
out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly to take the speck
out of your brother’s eye.” The City and County of Boulder are
suing Suncor and Exxon Mobil for knowingly driving climate change._

SOUTHWEST COLORADO HOUSING: HOUSE BILL 26-1001 LEFT PRIVATE BUILDERS
OUTSIDE THE GATE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

BY NAOMI RIESS, ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

_A teacher, nurse, deputy or young family should be able to buy a home
in Southwest Colorado. Too often, they look at the listings and

name: Mark Ronchetti
subject: Hull showed up. Haaland didn’t. Then the poll came out.
body:
Plus: Mark got some bad news about Bigfoot | New episode for dpwillis67@gmail.com

| | | | | |
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/13lF7BqjvM5?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
| | | | | |
On Thursday night, Gregg Hull stood on the KOB stage next to an empty podium. On Sunday, the Albuquerque Journal’s new poll had him 7 points behind the woman who didn’t show up. Mark thinks the race is closer than that 7 makes it look, and he walks through the numbers to show why.
In Texas, the Democrat running for a critical Senate just spent 13 days off the campaign trail. And Mark learned that the Bigfoot film he has always wanted to believe in may have been rehearsed... a year earlier.
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/fqXcL4j5pR1?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
| | **HAALAND LEADS HULL 49 TO 42 and HER OWN PARTY IS HER SOFT SPOT**
The Journal reached 1,125 people for this poll, all by phone, and that is why Mark takes it more seriously than most.
The real news is under the topline. Hull is doing better in the Albuquerque metro than Republicans did in last year’s mayor’s race, and Haaland holds fewer Democrats than Hull holds Republicans. That number should worry her even if she wins, and Mark says why.
Hull’s problem is independents, and money. We also play the two new attack ads in this race, and one of them uses a clip from our show.
---
| [STREAM NOW](https://us.list-manage.com/1D6OBTHQCEE?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
---
| | **TALARICO SPENT 13 DAYS OFF THE TRAIL, AND EL-SAYED WOULDN’T PICK ISRAEL OVER IRAN**
James Talarico’s campaign says he had the flu. Mark Penn, a Democratic strategist with 40 years in campaigns, says he has never seen a candidate do this in October.
In Michigan, Abdul El-Sayed was asked in a debate whether Israel or Iran is the bigger threat to the United States. He called it a ridiculous hypothetical. We play his answer and what a CNN panel said about it.

**🦶 A NEW DOCUMENTARY SAYS THE MOST FAMOUS BIGFOOT FILM WAS REHEARSED**
A reel shot in 1966, a year before the Patterson-Gimlin film, sat in a safe for decades. It shows a thinner Bigfoot walking through the woods and looking over its shoulder the same way.
Krysty broke the news to Mark on air. He had Grover Krantz as a professor at Washington State, and Krantz spent years arguing that a person could not easily fake that walk. Mark is not giving up until he sees the film.
---
| [STREAM NOW](https://us.list-manage.com/hlQZz1pZHGd?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
---
| | **PLUS:** Kansas is a toss-up for the U.S. Senate, Harry Enten shows where voters in four swing states are registering, and a mountain lion walked past our game camera at 11,000 feet. Also, name the movie on Mark’s shirt in the YouTube comments, and no Googling.

disclaimer_text: Paid For By Alex Vindman for Florida
body:
This is a ground game. This is person-to-person, human-to-human, mukluk telegraph.
Peter - Here’s my plan for how we win this election:
This is a ground game. This is person-to-person, human-to-human, mukluk telegraph.
For those in the Lower 48, mukluk telegraph is a saying we have in the Bush that basically amounts to gossip.
It’s passing along a message through our conversations with one another, _which is the only way information can really spread in some parts of the Last Frontier!_
In a state as vast and rural as ours, there really is no other way to reach every Alaskan. That’s why it’s so important for us to travel to their communities and have those person-to-person conversations.
There are 586,000 square miles in this state — bigger than Texas, California, and Montana combined. And we’re going to criss-cross it in its entirety.
But to be honest with you, reaching every community will be expensive.
More than 80% of our communities can only be reached by plane, boat or snow machine. And when we are able to drive, gas up here costs much more than it does in most of the Lower 48!
But we don’t have another option. I’m running for U.S. Senate to fight for all Alaskans, and I’m committed to bringing every borough into this fight with me.
That’s why I’m asking for your support today. We need to take our message across Alaska, and we can’t do it without your help.

Peter, Cait Conley here. This email isn’t going out to everyone tonight. It’s just going to a select crew of folks like you who have shown to be engaged and active members of this team. I need to ask a favor, and I’m hoping you’re someone who can help. In just two days, our campaign faces its final FEC deadline of the election, when we publicly release data on how much we’ve raised and from how many donors. NY-17 is going to be the most competitive and expensive House race in the country. Donald Trump is spending millions on ads here. So it’s really important that we be able to put out a strong report that shows we’re on track to push back on the dark money and beat Mike Lawler. People are going to be looking to gauge the strength of our campaign, and we cannot afford to come up short of our goals. That’s why I’m turning to you. body:
Democrats need the resources to fight back
---
Derek, this is an email from the Democratic National Committee about our work to flip Congress in 22 days. If you need help checking your voter registration or making a plan to vote, please visit [iwillvote.com](https://ak.democrats.org/go/9784?t=1&akid=9854%2E22930333%2E87WZI-). If you'd prefer to [receive fewer emails](https://ak.democrats.org/signup/receive-less-email/?t=2&akid=9854%2E22930333%2E87WZI-) or [stop receiving our emails](https://ak.democrats.org/cms/unsubscribe/unsubscribe/?t=3&akid=9854%2E22930333%2E87WZI-), you can click [here](https://ak.democrats.org/signup/receive-less-email/?t=4&akid=9854%2E22930333%2E87WZI-). Derek, here’s something about advertising you might not know: It books up. It’s a lot like trying to buy concert tickets — if a campaign wants to get their hands on primetime ad space in the run-up to Election Day, they need to book it _now_. **The very last day to reserve ad space is _October 29_.** That means time is running out for Democrats to get ads live and scale up their messaging operation. [**If that's all you need to hear, you can use this link to chip in $7 to the DNC and help campaigns make the most of these last couple of weeks.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-october-2026-gfr?refcode=em_20261012_9827_fr&amount=7&refcode2=9854_22930333_87WZI-&akid=9854%2E22930333%2E87WZI-) MAGA hasn’t missed the memo here: They’re spending _a billion dollars_ to flood the airwaves. Donald Trump is even _using taxpayer dollars_ to fund propaganda about himself while dark money groups buy ads to interrupt football games and spew hatred. **We’re suing Donald Trump and his administration to stop that — you can read more about that lawsuit[here](https://ak.democrats.org/go/89071?refcode=&t=5&akid=9854%2E22930333%2E87WZI-). But, in the meantime, we need to make sure that Democrats up and down the ballot, across the country, have the resources that they need to fight back.** Frankly, Democrats are running out of time to get ads on the air before Election Day. That’s why we need all hands on deck to make sure we leave no stone unturned when it comes to giving Democrats every chance at victory this November. If you’re wondering what you can do to help, the answer is simple. _You're getting this message because you’ve supported good causes and Democratic candidates. We need your support to continue fighting for our democracy. We love having you in our network, but if you only want our most important email updates,[click here.](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/108?t=2&akid=3477%2E259176%2EaTVR5T) If you'd like to unsubscribe, [click here.](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/109?t=3&akid=3477%2E259176%2EaTVR5T)_

[](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/18306?source=SL_EM_FR_2026.10.12_Flanagan-IDP_B4_F1_S1_C1_180AC-360DON&t=4&akid=3477%2E259176%2EaTVR5T) Today is Indigenous Peoples' Day, and I wanted to take a moment with you.

I am Ojibwe and a proud member of White Earth. My family is the Wolf Clan. The role of my clan is to never leave anyone behind — and that’s been my guiding principle throughout my entire life.

Today, I’m thinking of all our relatives who survived residential boarding schools. I’m thinking of my father, who always spoke truth to power for the good of the Anishinaabe people.

I’m thinking of my daughter — who just got her first jingle dress — and whether or not she will see Indigenous women in all parts of our government.

Above all, Indigenous people are resilient. We have always been here, and we will always be here. Today, I’m celebrating that.

_**But even now, there are no Native voices in the U.S. Senate.**_

It's high time that all our communities have a seat at the table. So I’m running to bring that resilience and strength to the United States Senate. [**On this Indigenous Peoples’ Day, will you split a donation between my campaign and Blue Amp Action to help us make history and build a future that serves all of us?**](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/18306?source=SL_EM_FR_2026.10.12_Flanagan-IDP_B4_F1_S1_C1_180AC-360DON&t=5&akid=3477%2E259176%2EaTVR5T) _If you've saved payment information with ActBlue Express, your split donation to Peggy Flanagan and Blue Amp Action will go through immediately:_ | [DONATE $12 >>](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/17726?source=SL_EM_FR_2026.10.12_Flanagan-IDP_B4_F1_S1_C1_180AC-360DON&t=6&akid=3477%2E259176%2EaTVR5T)

Today, I’m thinking of all our relatives who survived residential boarding schools. I’m thinking of my father, who always spoke truth to power for the good of the Anishinaabe people. I’m thinking of my daughter — who just got her first jingle dress — and whether or not she will see Indigenous women in all parts of our government. Above all, Indigenous people are resilient. We have always been here, and we will always be here. Today, I’m celebrating that. But even now, there are no Native voices in the U.S. Senate. It's high time that all our communities have a seat at the table. So I’m running to bring that resilience and strength to the United States Senate. Friend,
I just took the debate stage in Doraville, and you're the first person I wanted to talk to.
Here's what I took away from standing across from Keisha Lance Bottoms:
**She doesn't have a plan.**_**At all.**_
Not a bad plan. Not a plan I disagree with. No plan. Ask her a direct question about what she'd actually do for this state, and you get the same thing every time: **a practiced non-answer, a pivot, and a lot of words that add up to nothing.**
Georgians were watching. They deserved better than that.
What came through is that she'd run this state the way she ran Atlanta, and put Georgia LAST.
But I'm not writing to tell you what I think. I'm writing to hear what you think.

clean_body: The debate proved why Keisha Lance Bottoms is wrong for Georgia. | | | | | | | Untitled Document | | | | | | | ◆◆◆ | | Friend, I just took the debate stage in Doraville, and you're the first person I wanted to talk to. Here's what I took away from standing across from Keisha Lance Bottoms: She doesn't have a plan.At all. Not a bad plan. Not a plan I disagree with. No plan. Ask her a direct question about what she'd actually do for this state, and you get the same thing every time: a practiced non-answer, a pivot, and a lot of words that add up to nothing. Georgians were watching. They deserved better than that. What came through is that she'd run this state the way she ran Atlanta, and put Georgia LAST. But I'm not writing to tell you what I think. I'm writing to hear what you think. I'll tell you where I stand: I walked off that stage more determined than ever to win this election. Because the difference between the two of us isn't a debating style. It's whether the next Governor of Georgia is working for the people who live here, or for everybody else. I'm running to put Georgians FIRST. That's the whole thing. * Paid for by Jackson for Governor, Inc.

# [](https://act.electjon.com/go/4629?t=1&akid=3058%2E5691347%2EzZpOX-)

Jon Ossoff here.
I can guess what you’re thinking: _“great, another email asking me for money.”_

For the last two years, RFK Jr. and his political allies have operated under the assumption that they could sow doubt about basic public health, alter CDC guidance on a whim, and withhold vital healthcare funding without anyone in Washington calling them out on the actual data. They aren't used to dealing with scientists who hold legislative power. When RFK Jr. tries to swap peer-reviewed research for political deals or sideline independent public health panels, he relies on politicians who don't know the difference between a virus and a bacterium to just nod along. **He knows that when I get to Congress, he won't be dealing with a politician who can be easily misled by junk science. He’ll be answering to a scientist who spent her career studying infectious diseases, analyzing data, and teaching students to follow facts wherever they lead.** A virus doesn't check party registration, and disease doesn't care about political conspiracy theories. We desperately need evidence-based decision-making back in Washington to protect our families, our public health system, and our communities. RFK Jr. and anti-science special interests are pouring millions into holding onto power because they know what happens when scientists take a seat at the table: facts win. I’m proud to honor their work and the extraordinary legacy of Native peoples by leading a resolution in the Senate to recognize Indigenous Peoples’ Day and support making it a federal holiday. name: Elizabeth Warren (via Democrats.org)
subject: Derek, will you join me?
body:
Derek, I’m inviting you on an all-expenses paid trip to meet me.
---
Derek, this is an email from the Democratic National Committee about our work to flip Congress in 22 days. If you'd like to stop receiving emails about this contest, please [click here.](https://ak.democrats.org/signup/warren-sweepstakes-2026-opt-out/?t=1&akid=9821%2E22930333%2EgjioLX) | [](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-warren-sweepstakes-2026?amount=7&refcode=em_20261012_9821_fr&refcode2=9821_22930333_gjioLX&akid=9821%2E22930333%2EgjioLX)
---
**Derek, I’m inviting you on an all-expenses paid trip to meet me in Boston or DC.**[**Chip in $7, or any amount, to the DNC and you’ll be entered to win a free trip to meet me for you and a friend.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-warren-sweepstakes-2026?refcode=em_20261012_9821_fr&amount=7&refcode2=9821_22930333_gjioLX&akid=9821%2E22930333%2EgjioLX)
**[ENTER TO WIN](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-warren-sweepstakes-2026?refcode=em_20261012_9821_fr&amount=7&refcode2=9821_22930333_gjioLX&akid=9821%2E22930333%2EgjioLX)**
I’ve been doing everything I can to make sure Democrats win back majorities in the House and Senate this November, and as a member of the DNC’s Grassroots team, I know you have been, too. That’s why I want to meet you to say _thank you_ for all that you do.
**If Democrats win back our majorities, we can stop congressional Republicans from enabling the president.**
**We can block any far-right, extremist judge that Trump nominates to the Supreme Court.**
**And, critically, we can use those majorities to actually pass policies that you will _feel_ in your day-to-day life.**
I’ve done my homework: there is a narrow path to retake our majorities in Congress, but it can be done. We need to flip four seats to take back the Senate, which means we need to put up a strong defense in Michigan and Georgia, AND a strong offense in Maine, North Carolina, Iowa, Ohio, Texas, and Alaska.
But I _know_ Democrats can win if we have the resources to put up a fight. Grassroots supporters are the backbone of that fight.
Derek, we don’t have to wait until 2028 to stop Trump from using the presidency to enrich himself at the cost of you and your family. But I need you on board with me here if we’re going to achieve the ambitious wins it’s going to take to put a real check on his power. [**So, please, chip in $7, or any amount, to the DNC and enter to win a trip to meet me on the road so I can thank you for stepping up during the fight of our lives.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-warren-sweepstakes-2026?refcode=em_20261012_9821_fr&amount=7&refcode2=9821_22930333_gjioLX&akid=9821%2E22930333%2EgjioLX)

body:
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | |
---
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | **FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE****Date:** October 12, 2026 **Contact:**[ Taylor Gillespie](mailto:taylorg@eileenforcolorado.com), 720-557-6185
---
| |
# **Tonight, Retired Rear Admiral****Eileen Laubacher Puts Congresswoman Boebert on the Defense Over Her Failed Veterans, Rising Costs, Tariffs, and the Iran War in 9NEWS Debate **
---
| |

**HIGHLANDS RANCH, CO –** Tonight, Retired Rear Admiral Eileen Laubacher drew a sharp contrast between her 34 years of military service and Congresswoman Lauren Boebert’s time in Washington, making clear that Coloradans deserve a representative who puts their interests ahead of political rhetoric and partisan games.
Eileen blasted Boebert for voting to continue the war in Iran five times:

“**Congresswoman Boebert, of the two of us I believe only one of us has been to war.** If you believe no war is worth it then you should be voting against this war. And believe you me, no one knows more than I the cost of war. I have lost friends, many friends to wars. No part of me is ok with me when negotiations are on the table.”
[****](https://us.list-manage.com/TTcSGrnclL2?e=1c5f08419c&c2id=9f711ebcee4618a2092828a4c98e410a)
“You can say all day long that you don’t want there to be war and you want it to draw to a close, but you’re not using your voice to raise the voices of the people you describe in Congressional District 4 who are opposed to this war.**Your job is to be their voice in Congress, their voice to the President, saying we do not want this war, and you are failing to do that.”**
[****](https://us.list-manage.com/NAHlRI8mTMX?e=1c5f08419c&c2id=9f711ebcee4618a2092828a4c98e410a)
Eileen laid out the choice that Coloradans will make this fall:

“This November, Coloradans have a choice. We can continue with a representative who votes again and again to raise costs on Coloradans - 8 times for the tariffs that are costing Colorado families $4,200 out of their pockets, and 5 times for the Iran War that has sent gas and diesel prices skyrocketing – or we can fight for Coloradans instead. As a veteran, I have dedicated my life to service, and I’m ready to continue that commitment. I will fight to lower costs, support hardworking families, strengthen our agricultural industry, and build a Colorado that works for the many, not just the wealthy few.”
**###
**

body:
| | | **Donald Trump hosted a rally in Ohio tonight – and you can bet more money and more attacks are already coming our way. **

Here's the honest truth: Donald Trump is scared. He knows we have what it takes to win this race, and that what happens in Ohio will decide Senate control. That’s why he just made his second stop in Ohio this week. There is no issue of greater importance than addressing the accelerating global climate catastrophe. Yet policies established in Washington--on issues ranging from energy policy to foreign policy, farm subsidies, and trade policy--continue to actively make the climate crisis worse. Meanwhile, many leading Democrats have called to downplay those concerns to focus on less inconvenient alternatives.
## [Politics as mass delusion](https://substack.com/redirect/fe082423-e26c-4837-b7f3-53340281e4c4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
---
| | [Shahid Buttar](https://substack.com/profile/15484941-shahid-buttar)| | *
---|---|---
| Aug 12
[](https://substack.com/redirect/fe082423-e26c-4837-b7f3-53340281e4c4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[Apologists for the status quo, including the president, have long argued that climate change is a "hoax." Events unfolding around the world should convincingly disprove them, but even as related calamities continue to destroy lives and communities, America's corporate political parties continue to drag humanity towards a meteorological abyss with limitl...](https://substack.com/redirect/fe082423-e26c-4837-b7f3-53340281e4c4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
| [| Read full story

The uncomfortable reality is that Republicans and Democrats alike remain committed to burdening the future with ever-escalating threats to everything from coastal properties to crop yields.

The impacts are no longer looming years away.
### **Climate-related crises from coast-to-coast**
Residents of the Gulf Coast endured some of the impacts of anthropogenic global climate change this week. At least [four people died](https://substack.com/redirect/ecde69e9-4535-4d1c-b458-57907636d43d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in Alabama and Florida amid winds topping 100mph that literally tore the roofs from structures.
One of them, an apartment building in Milton, FL, became the subject of [a viral video](https://substack.com/redirect/bdda0ea2-8514-431b-aeaf-56a34f79dc70?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) depicting residents "huddled in fear as the roof over their heads was ripped away." As the storm made its way along the Atlantic coast, it generated [tornadoes](https://substack.com/redirect/5d5c100d-bad5-4854-97c7-fbe379c6559a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) from the Gulf of (checks notes) Mexico to South Carolina.
Hurricane Isias was [the first](https://substack.com/redirect/046812e2-a5eb-4e73-a23e-be8dddcb5a51?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Atlantic hurricane of a relatively quiet season, largely due to shifts in global heat distribution apparent in the [El Niño](https://substack.com/redirect/c70fae88-1ec1-408f-827e-811e26eb70cf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) phenomenon prompting mounting alarm up & down the West Coast. Referring to warmer-than-usual waters in the South Pacific, El Niño years often see suppressed hurricane activity in the Atlantic.
While Southern Californians experienced some impacts of the climate crisis [all summer](https://substack.com/redirect/fba61044-dff2-4c83-86ae-407944fdee1d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), the region is bracing for a [more predictable reckoning](https://substack.com/redirect/72db5770-081b-4b0c-a4ed-b4b9011083dc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) looming in a matter of weeks that could ironically include both floods and fires, in addition to coastal inundation and floods.
These are far from the first impacts our state has felt. California is still recovering from multiple climate-related disasters in the recent past, including [fires that devastated Los Angeles](https://substack.com/redirect/0cc42c2c-31d4-4797-8543-50c70bfe5635?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) less than a year ago, after [others that burned entire towns](https://substack.com/redirect/c5dad592-a0b2-46cf-87e0-8ac13494c70f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to the ground.
Some imagine that economic privilege might shield them & their families from the worst impacts of the climate catastrophe. What happened in Los Angeles last year exposed that pretense as a fallacy. As [I wrote](https://substack.com/redirect/75b11271-5b1e-4f83-b3f8-f30544f5749e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) at the time:
> "Before the wildfires burned the neighborhood to the ground, the median listing price of a home in Pacific Palisades was $4.7 million. An entire neighborhood of some of the richest people in the second largest city of the world's richest country just went up in flames.
>
> If that doesn't offer a wake up call to wealthy Americans in other cities to finally start prioritizing the needs of the future over their own bank accounts, nothing likely ever will."
## [The west coast wildfires reveal Washington's failures](https://substack.com/redirect/75b11271-5b1e-4f83-b3f8-f30544f5749e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

[I published an article yesterday reflecting on crises including the wildfires across Los Angeles. That post reflected on the unique international identity of Los Angeles, and the sad irony of cities on both coasts of the United States suffering climate disasters while Congress continues to sit on its hands, deferring to a predatory fossil fuel industry ...](https://substack.com/redirect/75b11271-5b1e-4f83-b3f8-f30544f5749e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

The graph below depicts the temperature in the South Pacific from January to December. Each year is a different line. Note that the line has never approached the current reading this early in the year.

### **A global crisis that Washington continues to ignore**
An El Niño of this magnitude portends any number of unfolding threats not only to California, but also communities--and crop supplies--around the world. "For example, effects from [past El Niño events](https://substack.com/redirect/27250b38-fe57-49d6-8972-6f3e0c625728?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) include flooding and landslides in Peru and California; forest fires and their ensuing air pollution in Indonesia; and droughts in northern Australia."
Experts at the University of Chicago's Climate Impact Lab have estimated that roughly [half a million people will die](https://substack.com/redirect/65d35f8b-44c5-4bac-b6b9-a0f57d223ddd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) from excessive heat alone--not even counting deaths resulting from storms, floods, fires, and collapsing crop yields.
The picture grows even more alarming when considering those predictable vectors for threats to communities.
In Britain, the Institute and Faculty of Actuaries is a professional body dedicated to educating and regulating actuaries, the insurance companies workers who quantitatively evaluate risk and establish (theoretically) commensurate insurance premiums. The Institute issued [a report in 2005](https://substack.com/redirect/6fbd0965-15a7-4fbb-b016-c9343b4c0296?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that warned of mounting risks to "planetary solvency," and a potential 50% contraction in global GDP.
The same report also warned of potentially _billions_ of deaths stemming from climate-related emergencies amounting to half of the human population of Earth. Those dire predictions inspired responses ranging from new climate organizations, such as [4 Billion Dead](https://substack.com/redirect/126f6d27-dc32-4b7c-ba90-4d18a068336c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), to corresponding [critiques](https://substack.com/redirect/9affc766-58d0-4e02-ba01-6fb3c702febf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) raising issues with how the report's alarming findings have been publicly described.
People who study risk for a living are forecasting mass deaths in a range that no one should be willing to accept. Yet, after decades of governmental deference to predatory industry, none of us have any effective choice remaining in the matter.
### **How to respond in the face of catastrophe**
When people wonder whether the world as we know it might end, it's worth remembering that it already did for plenty of people. [I included a poem exploring this theme in one of my previous posts, which I've spent the better part of an hour trying to track down to no avail. I'll update this post to include the link if I ever find it again.]
Indigenous communities have faced existential risks before. While many may appear to have been entirely destroyed, the resilience demonstrated by those who survive might offer important clues for the rest of us.
Reflecting on Indigenous Peoples Day, Nabila Mella Garip [wrote](https://substack.com/redirect/97593b02-5796-44b5-824e-f0e4147cf6f7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) two years ago that:
> Although most aspects of Indigenous cultures were deliberately obliterated by European colonizers (artifacts destroyed, languages suppressed, religions forcibly replaced by Christianity), there is still vibrant Indigenous life....
> In the Caribbean, the vast majority of indigenous peoples were exterminated (or so we've been told). However, it is interesting to note that [DNA studies have shown](https://substack.com/redirect/bcb841c3-09c9-4513-896d-1ffa48ec6507?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that 61% of Puerto Ricans, 23-30% of Dominicans, and 33% of Cubans have indigenous DNA markers (even though their Indigenous populations were exterminated centuries ago).
> Indigenous peoples have immense knowledge about how to live in communion with nature because in many cases, they believe themselves to be a part of it. With foreign influences, especially from the US, many communities are leaving behind this balanced and connected way of thinking -- and it is high time we reclaim it. (emphases removed)
Indigenous conceptions of connectedness to land offer one perspective that might offer, if not hope, at least something resembling solace. A generation of eco-activists might have implored our society to "save the Earth," which will inevitably be just fine. The Earth was here before people, and it will remain, regardless of what we do to it and ourselves.
But will the Earth continue to sustain human life? It is not the planet for which we need to fear, but rather our grandchildren.
One writer on this platform [thoughtfully suggested](https://substack.com/redirect/96b22ea9-5c9c-48f7-b87c-e15e423d1774?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that:
> [W]hile the powerful sell us the fantasy of green growth and endless techno-solutions, it is frontline communities who are treating this crisis like the emergency it is, often without resources, recognition, or time to rest. And...there is still no other solution today that has protected more biodiversity, or prevented more emissions, than Indigenous land defenders.
The story of indigenous communities defending land from colonial exploitation is not confined to history. It continues today, with new flash points denominating both the struggles and their victories.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9ec2c889-434c-43c2-baad-d514a1fcd4ce?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Image from https://observanceguide.com/indigenous-peoples-day-2026/
As data centers claim increasing swaths of land and water around the country, while also promoting a technology with limitless risks, the leading edges of resistance are indigenous tribes. The Cherokee Nation, Seminole Nation, and Kickapoo Tribe have all halted data center construction on tribal lands covering 8,000 square miles. They were joined this month by the Cheyenne and Arapaho tribes.
[| | | Shahid Buttar 6dRecognizing and respecting indigenous wisdom might just be the key to the rest of the country saving itself...from itself.
---
https://substack.com/@moreperfectus/note/c-354290508
| 17| 2| 3|
---|---|---|---](https://substack.com/profile/15484941-shahid-buttar/note/c-354663132)
Indigenous communities, by blocking data centers to protect the Earth and its inhabitants, are offering the same leadership that they did when resisting the colonial [mass murder of animals](https://substack.com/redirect/b7badeef-96fd-4823-b87e-9abadc89e4e1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and [deforestation](https://substack.com/redirect/5381b14c-a7c1-4c50-992b-86f482308843?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
Our society was too ignorant to recognize the value of that leadership in the past. Have we learned anything from it, or are we instead doomed to repeat the cycle of ignoring indigenous wisdom until (whoever survives among) our grandchildren eventually figure it out?

Chronicles of a Dying Empire is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts,sign up for a free subscription! Paid subscriptions help support & expand my work. The impacts are no longer looming years away. Climate-related crises from coast-to-coast Residents of the Gulf Coast endured some of the impacts of anthropogenic global climate change this week. At least in Alabama and Florida amid winds topping 100mph that literally tore the roofs from structures. One of them, an apartment building in Milton, FL, became the subject of depicting residents "huddled in fear as the roof over their heads was ripped away." As the storm made its way along the Atlantic coast, it generated from the Gulf of (checks notes) Mexico to South Carolina. Hurricane Isias was Atlantic hurricane of a relatively quiet season, largely due to shifts in global heat distribution apparent in the phenomenon prompting mounting alarm up & down the West Coast. Referring to warmer-than-usual waters in the South Pacific, El Niño years often see suppressed hurricane activity in the Atlantic. While Southern Californians experienced some impacts of the climate crisis , the region is bracing for a looming in a matter of weeks that could ironically include both floods and fires, in addition to coastal inundation and floods. These are far from the first impacts our state has felt. California is still recovering from multiple climate-related disasters in the recent past, including less than a year ago, after to the ground. Some imagine that economic privilege might shield them & their families from the worst impacts of the climate catastrophe. What happened in Los Angeles last year exposed that pretense as a fallacy. As at the time: "Before the wildfires burned the neighborhood to the ground, the median listing price of a home in Pacific Palisades was $4.7 million. An entire neighborhood of some of the richest people in the second largest city of the world's richest country just went up in flames. If that doesn't offer a wake up call to wealthy Americans in other cities to finally start prioritizing the needs of the future over their own bank accounts, nothing likely ever will." | | | | ---|---|--- | January 14, 2025 | The El Niño brewing in the South Pacific this autumn is . The graph below depicts the temperature in the South Pacific from January to December. Each year is a different line. Note that the line has never approached the current reading this early in the year. A global crisis that Washington continues to ignore An El Niño of this magnitude portends any number of unfolding threats not only to California, but also communities--and crop supplies--around the world. "For example, effects from include flooding and landslides in Peru and California; forest fires and their ensuing air pollution in Indonesia; and droughts in northern Australia." Experts at the University of Chicago's Climate Impact Lab have estimated that roughly from excessive heat alone--not even counting deaths resulting from storms, floods, fires, and collapsing crop yields. The picture grows even more alarming when considering those predictable vectors for threats to communities. In Britain, the Institute and Faculty of Actuaries is a professional body dedicated to educating and regulating actuaries, the insurance companies workers who quantitatively evaluate risk and establish (theoretically) commensurate insurance premiums. The Institute issued that warned of mounting risks to "planetary solvency," and a potential 50% contraction in global GDP. The same report also warned of potentially billions of deaths stemming from climate-related emergencies amounting to half of the human population of Earth. Those dire predictions inspired responses ranging from new climate organizations, such as , to corresponding raising issues with how the report's alarming findings have been publicly described. People who study risk for a living are forecasting mass deaths in a range that no one should be willing to accept. Yet, after decades of governmental deference to predatory industry, none of us have any effective choice remaining in the matter. How to respond in the face of catastrophe When people wonder whether the world as we know it might end, it's worth remembering that it already did for plenty of people. [I included a poem exploring this theme in one of my previous posts, which I've spent the better part of an hour trying to track down to no avail. I'll update this post to include the link if I ever find it again.] Indigenous communities have faced existential risks before. While many may appear to have been entirely destroyed, the resilience demonstrated by those who survive might offer important clues for the rest of us. Reflecting on Indigenous Peoples Day, Nabila Mella Garip two years ago that: Although most aspects of Indigenous cultures were deliberately obliterated by European colonizers (artifacts destroyed, languages suppressed, religions forcibly replaced by Christianity), there is still vibrant Indigenous life.... In the Caribbean, the vast majority of indigenous peoples were exterminated (or so we've been told). However, it is interesting to note that that 61% of Puerto Ricans, 23-30% of Dominicans, and 33% of Cubans have indigenous DNA markers (even though their Indigenous populations were exterminated centuries ago). Indigenous peoples have immense knowledge about how to live in communion with nature because in many cases, they believe themselves to be a part of it. With foreign influences, especially from the US, many communities are leaving behind this balanced and connected way of thinking -- and it is high time we reclaim it. (emphases removed) Indigenous conceptions of connectedness to land offer one perspective that might offer, if not hope, at least something resembling solace. A generation of eco-activists might have implored our society to "save the Earth," which will inevitably be just fine. The Earth was here before people, and it will remain, regardless of what we do to it and ourselves. But will the Earth continue to sustain human life? It is not the planet for which we need to fear, but rather our grandchildren. One writer on this platform that: [W]hile the powerful sell us the fantasy of green growth and endless techno-solutions, it is frontline communities who are treating this crisis like the emergency it is, often without resources, recognition, or time to rest. And...there is still no other solution today that has protected more biodiversity, or prevented more emissions, than Indigenous land defenders. The story of indigenous communities defending land from colonial exploitation is not confined to history. It continues today, with new flash points denominating both the struggles and their victories. | | ---|---|--- Image from As data centers claim increasing swaths of land and water around the country, while also promoting a technology with limitless risks, the leading edges of resistance are indigenous tribes. The Cherokee Nation, Seminole Nation, and Kickapoo Tribe have all halted data center construction on tribal lands covering 8,000 square miles. They were joined this month by the Cheyenne and Arapaho tribes. Indigenous communities, by blocking data centers to protect the Earth and its inhabitants, are offering the same leadership that they did when resisting the colonial and . Our society was too ignorant to recognize the value of that leadership in the past. Have we learned anything from it, or are we instead doomed to repeat the cycle of ignoring indigenous wisdom until (whoever survives among) our grandchildren eventually figure it out? subject: A memo just for Derek:
body:
My team and I put this together specifically for our top supporters — including you.
---
Derek, this is an email from the Democratic National Committee about our work to flip Congress in 21 days. If you need help checking your voter registration or making a plan to vote, please visit [iwillvote.com](https://ak.democrats.org/go/9784?t=1&akid=9828%2E22930333%2EduWYOg). If you'd prefer to [receive fewer emails](https://ak.democrats.org/signup/receive-less-email/?t=2&akid=9828%2E22930333%2EduWYOg) or [stop receiving our emails](https://ak.democrats.org/cms/unsubscribe/unsubscribe/?t=3&akid=9828%2E22930333%2EduWYOg), you can click [here](https://ak.democrats.org/signup/receive-less-email/?t=4&akid=9828%2E22930333%2EduWYOg). Derek, it’s DNC Chair Ken Martin here. You’re one of our most engaged supporters, so it’s important to me that we keep you updated on what the DNC is doing to elect Democrats to win back Congress and countless other offices across the country. **That’s why I’m writing to you today with this exclusive midterm strategy memo. Please take a few minutes to read it if you can.** \--------------------------------------------------
**To:** Derek Willis**
**From:** The Desk of the DNC Chair, Ken Martin
**Date:** October 13th, 2026
**Subject:** State-of-the-Midterms Update There are just under three weeks until Election Day, and Democrats have a real chance at taking back control of both the House and Senate this November. Here’s what we’re doing to make that happen:
* **Democrats need to flip four Republican-held seats to win the Senate.** A Democratic Senate majority would shatter Donald Trump’s trifecta and make sure he _never_ gets to appoint another right-wing hack to the Supreme Court again. That’s why the DNC is sending record-breaking investments to Democratic state parties: to help them make the biggest voter contact push in midterm history and flip these seats.
* **The DNC is mobilizing more than one million Americans to fight back against GOP billionaires attempting to buy our democracy.** GOP megadonors and super PACs plan to spend nearly **1 BILLION dollars** in House, Senate, and down-ballot races to ensure that Republicans keep their trifecta. They know that if Democrats win control of Congress, their far-right agenda will come to a screeching halt. But while Republicans have MAGA billionaires on their side, our movement is powered by hardworking Americans — teachers, nurses, and truck drivers — who are pitching in an average of $34.32 at a time to support our efforts and help us build the infrastructure necessary for Democrats to win.
* **The DNC is countering the influx of MAGA attack ads with direct digital outreach.** For years, people have asked when Democrats will step up their online presence. We’ve done just that. The DNC has a brilliant team of social media strategists working to expose Trump’s and MAGA’s lies online. We just recently reached 14.4 million total followers and generated over 1 billion impressions across social media platforms. This massive organic and targeted online reach allows us to bypass legacy media channels and communicate directly with swing voters and grassroots supporters alike.
* **The DNC is putting boots on the ground and organizing in key battleground states.** Through specialized training bootcamps, sharing our DNC Campaign Playbook, hiring campaign fellows, and hosting local listening tours, we’ve trained hundreds of field organizers, registered tens of thousands of voters, and empowered Democratic state parties and campaign staff to fight and win next month.

\--------------------------------------------------
Derek, if this update was helpful, and if winning back Congress matters to you, [**please chip in a $7 contribution to the DNC today. We’ll put your donation to work immediately to fund all the work I just told you about — and more — to elect Democrats across the country.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-october-2026-gfr?amount=7&refcode=em_20261013_9828_fr&refcode2=9828_22930333_duWYOg&akid=9828%2E22930333%2EduWYOg) _If you 've stored your info with ActBlue, we'll process your contribution instantly._ | | | **[Donate $7](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-october-2026-gfr?express_lane=true&amount=7&refcode=em_20261013_9828_fr&refcode2=9828_22930333_duWYOg&akid=9828%2E22930333%2EduWYOg)**

body:
# [](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/188?t=1&akid=2516%2E135344%2EwJxUUN)

As Republicans search for ways to save the Senate, they've set their sights on New Hampshire. Take a look:
[](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/9?c0=ebs-em-pappas-split._m_z_j&refcode=em261013&t=2&akid=2516%2E135344%2EwJxUUN)
[](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/9?c0=ebs-em-pappas-split._m_z_j&refcode=em261013&t=3&akid=2516%2E135344%2EwJxUUN)
One seat.
If Republicans can flip one Democratic Senate seat in this election, all of the possibilities we have in places like Alaska, Texas, Iowa, Kansas and more may be all for naught when it comes to taking back the Senate.
Republicans are looking at New Hampshire for that seat.
Already, there's been more than $50 million in outside spending in that race. And it is not as if New Hampshire is a huge state with several large media markets.
The good news is this: all of those outside spending groups have to pay a higher rate for television advertising than Chris Pappas does.
That means every dollar Chris raises is worth 3, 4, 5 times-plus more than Republican super PACs.
So if Democrats are going to take back the Senate, New Hampshire is a place we need to shore-up our defenses. And that is why Elissa wanted to ask:
[**Can you please split a contribution between Chris Pappas' campaign for Senate and Elissa Slotkin's work helping to elect Democrats everywhere. Early voting is underway, and it is time to **stand up** , **show up** , and **defend our state**.Voting is just the beginning. Through **Tusk Force** , Republicans across Indiana are knocking on doors, reaching voters, and working to deliver victories up and down the ballot. [**Join Tusk Force today**](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-fdrkjdl-hhlljjcji-r/) and help get our Republican ticket across the finish line.We are fortunate to live in a country where citizens choose their own representatives, but self-governance only works when people participate. _" A republic, if you can keep it."_ Now is the time to defend that republic and the principles we hold dear here in Indiana.As Republicans, we stand for limited government, individual liberty, common sense, and accountability to the public. But defending those principles requires Hoosiers willing to fight for them at the ballot box.**Let me be clear: Our livelihoods hang in the balance.** This election, we have a strong statewide Republican ticket in **Max Engling for Secretary of State, Comptroller Elise Nieshalla, and Treasurer Daniel Elliott.** Alongside Republican candidates across Indiana, we are fighting to keep our state moving forward and deliver results for Hoosier families.Don't let anyone tell you this election doesn't matter. The leaders we elect will shape our property taxes, economic opportunities, schools, public safety, and the future we leave to the next generation.**Your vote matters, and every Republican must cast theirs.** Whether you vote early or on Election Day, **November 3** , make a commitment to vote. And if you live in a county where "everyone is Republican," don't assume your vote doesn't matter. Our rural communities must turn out to overcome the Democrats in Indianapolis.Indiana may be a predominantly Republican state, but if we don't show up, we risk losing the principles and policies we've fought to protect. Find your polling location, make a plan, and encourage your friends and family to vote. _This is your civic duty._**Ready to take the next step?** With just **22 days until Election Day** , every door knocked, every conversation, and every vote matters.[**Join Tusk Force**](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-fdrkjdl-hhlljjcji-y/) and help carry our Republican ticket across the finish line.Indiana's future belongs to the Hoosiers who show up. **Make your plan, bring a friend, and vote Republican!** _Indiana Republican Party Political Director, Ethan Bailey_ [](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-fdrkjdl-hhlljjcji-j/)[](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-fdrkjdl-hhlljjcji-t/)[](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-fdrkjdl-hhlljjcji-i/)[](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-fdrkjdl-hhlljjcji-d/)[](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-fdrkjdl-hhlljjcji-h/)[](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-fdrkjdl-hhlljjcji-k/) ** PAID FOR BY THE INDIANA REPUBLICAN STATE COMMITTEE. ****NOT AUTHORIZED BY ANY CANDIDATE OR CANDIDATE'S COMMITTEE. ****WWW.INDIANA.GOP.** | Indiana Republican State Committee 101 W. disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY VOTEVETS, VOTEVETS
body:
#
Peter,
As you’ve seen by now, Pete Hegseth announced that the execution of Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan will be publicly livestreamed — the first time our government has ever broadcast an execution publicly — and the plan was greenlit by Donald Trump.
Thirteen Americans were killed and dozens injured that day. No one disputes that they deserve justice. But Pete Hegseth wants to make this execution into a media spectacle, taking a page from the very same terrorist groups the mass murderer was inspired by. He wants to make this about Hasan, when it should be about the people who were killed and wounded that day.
VoteVets refuses to stay silent. So today, we’re releasing a new video.
**Army Staff Sgt. Paul Martin (ret.) survived the Fort Hood mass shooting, and he is slamming Hegseth’s plan to livestream the execution. You can watch it here:**

VoteVets

body:
Poll after poll shows me tied with Susan Collins, and she’s spending double what we are on TV ads. We need to pick up the pace if we want any shot at flipping this seat and retaking the Senate majority for Democrats.
#
Peter, here’s the deal.
Susan Collins really knows how to put on a show in the Senate.
She votes with Trump 96% of the time. If she knows one of his bad bills is going to tank, she’ll vote against it. If she’s the deciding vote, she’ll always vote for it, just like how she was the deciding vote for Brett Kavanaugh, who then overturned _Roe v. Wade._
The same is also true with Trump’s tariffs. Mainers and folks across the country are hurting badly from rising costs – and too many families are having to pick between picking up their prescriptions or putting food on the table.
So when she said during our debate that she brought down the cost of road salt, **I had to say what shouldn’t need to be said:**
[](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/109729?refcode=em20261013-11008&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1&akid=11008%2E614464%2EnK26ek)
It goes to show just how out of touch Susan is with families across Maine. Road salt isn’t going to make groceries, heating oil, or everyday necessities affordable again.
Susan Collins is so used to putting the needs of billionaires over her constituents. I’m running to defeat her because folks across Maine have made me into the public servant I am today, and they deserve a Senator who isn’t afraid to take on tough battles.
**But poll after poll shows me tied with Susan Collins, and she’s spending double what we are on TV ads. We need to pick up the pace if we want any shot at flipping this seat and retaking the Senate majority for Democrats.**
**[So Peter, will you please split $15 – or more, if you can spare it – between my campaign and State Democrats Committee right now? I refuse to take a dime from corporate PACs (unlike Susan), so I can’t run my campaign without folks like you chipping in.](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/109729?refcode=em20261013-11008&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=2&akid=11008%2E614464%2EnK26ek)**

At the GOP Senate debate, John Sununu told a roomful of Republicans he’s
running to send me back to “bussing tables” at my family’s “chicken
restaurant.” He meant it as an insult.

As if the people who work in restaurants — cooking your food, clearing
your plates, keeping family businesses alive — have something to be
embarrassed about.

My great-grandfather came to New Hampshire from Greece over a century ago
and opened a candy shop in Manchester. My family built it into a
restaurant that’s been serving our community ever since.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261013_2.ourP2C&refcode=em20261013-2&t=1003&akid=9500%2E582294%2ETd67xV ]Puritan Backroom sign

John Sununu was born into a political dynasty. His father was governor and
White House Chief of Staff. His brother was governor. John went to
Washington and then spent the next 17 years cashing in with Big Oil, Big
Pharma, and Wall Street.

Oh, and his family business invested in a literal gold mine in Azerbaijan
that sells minerals to China. He’s never had to work hard a day in his
life — and his comments at that debate prove exactly what he thinks of
people who do.

The people who bus tables, flip burgers, and run small businesses in New
Hampshire don’t need a senator who looks down on them. They need one who
comes from them.

running for Senate.

Loomer Unleashed recently [reported](https://substack.com/redirect/ad64d2c9-1d55-41bb-9a4b-7d46e74677e2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that Weichai Group, a Chinese state-owned conglomerate that was founded to make rifles for the People's Liberation Army, had seized control of Ferretti Group, one of the biggest yacht builders in the world. I told you that Weichai executives had talked openly about moving Ferretti's production technology to a new marine hub in Qingdao, the city that hosts the headquarters of the PLA Navy's Northern Theater Command and a submarine base.
Now I can show you the shipyard with exclusive images.
Loomer Unleashed has obtained satellite images of Weichai's Qingdao facility, along with construction photographs and footage that Weichai and Chinese state media released inside China and never intended for an American audience to see. The images show that Communist China has already built a full-scale shipyard with an 80-meter production line, ship lifts, and a 458-meter outfitting facility. It is finished, and it is sitting almost empty, waiting for Italian technology to arrive.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/129281fb-3c75-4943-98a5-d45bc326dff9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The facility is officially called the Weichai (Qingdao) High-End Marine Equipment Manufacturing Center. It sits at 269-5 Changjiang East Road in Xuejiadao, on the west shore of an inlet in Qingdao's West Coast New Area. The operating company is Bostar Marine Technology (Qingdao), [which was incorporated on January 19, 2022](https://substack.com/redirect/2142e1a8-ca5c-41ce-af22-6fb317f3046c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Three weeks later, on February 8, 2022, [Weichai broke ground on the site](https://substack.com/redirect/9d6e8dae-f116-4535-8f52-88cb0ebe0004?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) as the headline project in a batch of [125 spring construction projects announced by the local government](https://substack.com/redirect/d0655c60-611c-44cd-b309-af5ebe31ad8b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/216d1b02-e0d4-4957-b5cd-c10996e6a094?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/3be5340c-fefa-4ceb-839b-ee59bb0b3b8e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Building out some of the facility was contracted to China Construction Port and [reported by Qingdao's municipal media as a public infrastructure project](https://substack.com/redirect/9e9606ed-a627-45d7-9180-cdeedbe3a096?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). [According to Qingdao Daily](https://substack.com/redirect/74519ef8-0f6d-4146-b320-b45e4d86c065?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), the specification called for a 458-meter outfitting quay (a specialized waterfront dock where new vessels are finalized) with six outfitting berths. In other words, the Chinese state helped build the dock for a yacht company it would later take over.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/8a2e8e01-1773-4c1d-9fee-f102da1bfe0b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/11178d86-cf74-4cda-83d4-b06f15d93864?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c7adf0b4-b247-4645-b78a-004e1219653c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/401a619c-16a0-4441-aad8-8536aacac738?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
On March 10, 2025, Weichai Power published a 98-second promotional [film](https://substack.com/redirect/71e7e31d-b1e5-426e-b67e-2c654bd61c29?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) titled "'New' Heavy Industry," presented by a young employee walking through the plant. Weichai said the steel and aluminum boat-building halls were basically complete and that the plant would be ready for production by the end of March 2025. The film is the only published look inside the facility.
